tooling-rules.mandate: These rules are NON-NEGOTIABLE for all review work on this project. Use these tools to VERIFY implementation correctness.

skills-mandatory.desc: Skills that MUST be activated during code review
skills-mandatory.skill: Monorepo and build pipeline management. Verify turbo.json pipelines, workspace dependencies, and build correctness.
React and Next.js performance optimization. Review ALL React components and Next.js pages for performance anti-patterns.
Production-grade "Clinique Zen" interface standards. Verify UI components meet design system quality and aesthetic requirements.
Automated browser testing and visual validation. Use to verify UI rendering, interaction flows, and catch visual regressions.

mcp-servers.desc: MCP servers to use during review verification
mcp-servers.server: Up-to-date documentation retrieval for ALL libraries. Use to verify implementations follow current API patterns and best practices for Prisma, NestJS, tRPC, Zsa, next-intl, Stripe, shadcn/ui, dnd-kit, etc.
Fast file operations for bulk reads across the monorepo during review.

plugins.desc: Claude plugins to use during review
plugins.plugin: Stripe best practices, test card numbers, and error code explanations. Use to verify Stripe integration follows security best practices (HMAC, idempotency, raw body parser isolation).

review-enforcement.rule: Verify library-specific code matches latest documentation via context7 - flag outdated patterns as HIGH findings.
Check React/Next.js code against vercel-react-best-practices - flag performance anti-patterns.
Validate UI components against frontend-design "Clinique Zen" standards - flag aesthetic violations.
Verify monorepo structure and build config against turborepo best practices.
Use agent-browser to visually verify UI changes when the application is running.
For Stripe-related code, verify against stripe plugin best practices (webhook security, PCI compliance).

parallel-execution-rules.mandate: Use Claude Code's Task tool and TodoWrite to orchestrate review and fix work efficiently.
When fixing multiple independent issues, launch parallel sub-agents to maximize throughput.
parallel-execution-rules.rule: When a review finds 3+ issues to fix, create a task list (TaskCreate) to track each fix. Update task status (TaskUpdate) as fixes are applied: pending → in_progress → completed. Present the task list to the user for visibility on progress.

During the review phase (Step 3), launch parallel sub-agents to review different aspects simultaneously: - One agent for AC validation (acceptance criteria vs implementation) - One agent for code quality deep dive (security, performance, patterns) - One agent for test quality assessment This reduces review time significantly.

When fixing multiple independent issues (Step 4, user chooses "Fix automatically"): - Group fixes by file: all edits to the same file go to ONE agent - Launch independent file-group agents in parallel with run_in_background=true - Wait for all agents to complete before proceeding to status update - Never let two agents edit the same file simultaneously

Use specialized sub-agent types: - subagent_type="feature-dev:code-reviewer" for deep review analysis - subagent_type="code-simplifier:code-simplifier" for focused file fixes - subagent_type="Explore" for codebase research during review - subagent_type="Bash" for build/test verification after fixes

The story documentation update task (Dev Agent Record, Change Log, Status History) should always run LAST, after all code fixes are confirmed complete. Use TaskUpdate addBlockedBy to enforce this dependency.
